why: User-provided information decides the interaction: whether an answer may be asserted, whether research must run first, and whether a stale or contradicted fact has to be reconciled. Without a declared table the same input could be answered directly in one path and researched in another, and the epistemic states would quietly collapse into a guess. The daemon layer proposes; it does not dispatch — the shipped dialogue schema already pins `dispatch_requested` to false.

bindings.speech_acts: drivers/daemon-dialogue/daemon-dialogue.v1.schema.json (#/properties/speech_act) — the same nine acts, reused rather than reinvented
bindings.dialogue_does_not_dispatch: the dialogue schema declares `dispatch_requested: const false`, so a mode may propose effects but not perform them

daemon_modes.direct: answer from already-covered, fresh, evidenced knowledge
daemon_modes.assist: compose fields or propose one-line fixes from covered knowledge; assert nothing new
daemon_modes.research: gather external evidence before anything is asserted
daemon_modes.verify: fact-check a claim that arrived without evidence (a hypothesis is never self-certifying)
daemon_modes.reconcile: a correction or conflict against stored knowledge: resolve, never silently overwrite
daemon_modes.clarify: the input does not determine an answer: ask, and keep the state UNKNOWN

selection_law.law: the mode is a deterministic function of the user's information: speech act, topic coverage, freshness, whether it conflicts with stored knowledge, and whether evidence came with it
order: 1. a conflict with stored knowledge, an objection or a disagreement → reconcile
2. a request for current information, or a stale fact → research
3. a hypothesis → verify (never assert from its own statement)
4. a proposal → assist (compose or propose, assert nothing)
5. a question or intent analysis over covered, fresh, evidenced knowledge → direct
6. an evidence report over covered fresh knowledge → direct
7. an agreement or final answer that is covered, fresh and evidenced → direct
8. anything else → clarify, and the state stays UNKNOWN
selection_law.determinism: rule order is part of the contract: applying the same information always selects the same mode

epistemic_states.law: these never collapse: only SUPPORTED may be asserted, MISS carries a research plan instead of an answer, UNKNOWN asks rather than guesses, and CONTRADICTED reconciles rather than overwrites

mapping.reconcile: CONTRADICTED when the conflict is unevidenced, UNKNOWN when it is being resolved

online_update_events.law: an online event signals that information has moved on; it invalidates only the topics it covers
online_update_events.stale: a covered, affected topic becomes stale and must be re-researched before it is used again
online_update_events.contradicted: an event that supersedes prior information marks the covered topic CONTRADICTED rather than merely stale
online_update_events.no_op: an uncovered topic is a no-op: an update signal never invalidates knowledge it says nothing about
online_update_events.downstream: a stale or contradicted topic blocks composition until it is re-researched

effects.law: the three effects are the only things a session may do with what it learned, and each is gated independently

compose_field.requires: SUPPORTED knowledge and a fresh topic; a stale or unsupported topic may not be composed into a field
compose_field.produces: a proposal (see src/world/asx_field.h key → field expansion)

update_gap.requires: evidence and a legal transition; closing a gap needs its validation command, so an unevidenced claim cannot mark anything Resolved

fix_one_liner.requires: admission; a session proposes the edit and another layer applies it, because the dialogue schema declares dispatch_requested false

invariants.IM1: only SUPPORTED may be asserted; MISS carries a research plan, UNKNOWN asks, and CONTRADICTED reconciles — the four states never collapse into one answer
invariants.IM2: a request for current information, or a stale fact, forces research before any assertion
invariants.IM3: a hypothesis is verified, never asserted from its own statement
invariants.IM4: a user correction that conflicts with stored knowledge reconciles; it never silently overwrites
invariants.IM5: an online event invalidates only the topics it covers, and an uncovered topic is a no-op
invariants.IM6: composing a field requires SUPPORTED knowledge and a fresh topic; composition from stale or unevidenced knowledge is refused
invariants.IM7: a gap update requires evidence and a legal transition: without them the state does not move
invariants.IM8: a one-line fix is proposed, never applied, without admission — the dialogue layer declares dispatch_requested false and so does this layer
